ops.title: Deployment recovery ergonomics: no fresh-install reset verb — incoherent state needs three manual move-asides
ops.description:
Recovering the local captain-hook deployment (2026-07-26) after cleared quiesce receipts required walking three fail-closed guards by hand, each individually correct:

1. `ErrVersionMismatch` — a stale staged candidate (`.Captain Hook.daemonkit-candidate.app` at 12.20.11) is validated against the requested version instead of being superseded/re-delivered.
2. `install path conflict: installed app exists without sealed activation` — the installed (orphaned) app is never adopted.
3. `install path conflict: absent app has retained deployment state` — leftover deactivation.json/services.db block fresh install even with the app gone.

Sequence that worked: move candidate aside → move installed app aside → move the whole per-app deployment-state dir aside → `capt-hookd package-install` fresh-installs cleanly (12.20.12, sealed receipts, keyless agents). Every guard fired exactly as designed; what's missing is a single deliberate recovery verb (e.g. `deployment reset --retire-installed`) that retires candidate + app + retained state coherently (backing them up) so operators don't improvise the ordering. A stale same-name candidate with a DIFFERENT version could also plausibly be superseded automatically on delivery rather than refused.

ops.text: A documented single-verb (or single-flow) recovery path exists for an incoherent deployment, covering stale candidate, orphaned installed app, and retained state
